query: With apex26.gfxBackend set to webgl2, the game canvas comes up completely black after picking Monza, but the HUD still renders. Console shows GL_INVALID_OPERATION from a draw call in js/render/glx/glx.js. Please diagnose which pass or state is at fault and fix it.
glx sun shadows have nasty acne stripes on the tarmac when the sun is low, and also the shadow edges look super blocky. can u figure out whats wrong w/ the shadow map bias n fix it

On the WebGL2 path the whole scene goes blown-out white whenever the bloom pass runs, especially near bright floodlights, but it looks fine with bloom off. Something about HDR? Find why the GPU bloom is over-strong and correct it.

I raised MAX_LIGHTS in js/render/glx/shaders/glsl-lit.js and now the fragment shader fails to compile on some drivers with a uniform-array size complaint, and lamps past a certain index don't light the road. Help me track down the uniform limit problem.

Sometimes at boot the explicit WebGL2 backend reports hdrMode as off on a device that should support float render targets, so the ACES tone-map output looks banded. Check the HDR availability probe in the GLX renderer and confirm whether the fallback format path is correct.
Night races look washed out and grey, like daytime, and the floodlights don't seem to turn on at dusk. Ambient and exposure sliders barely change it. Figure out which lighting knob or gate is wrong.

The WebGPU backend shows a black screen and the console has a WGSL compile error about a bind group layout, then it silently falls back to WebGL2 with the bloom pass still fine. Diagnose the WGSL validation failure.
While driving through the Spa pit straight the road surface shimmers and z-fights with the kerb shadow overlay. Record a driven clip and capture frames so we can see the flicker frame by frame.

With apex26.gfxBackend set to webgpu, the race scene renders black on Chrome 140 and the console shows a WGSL validation error out of js/render/webgpu/wgsl-post.js. Find the failing shader, fix it, and confirm it compiles under real Dawn before I ship.
wgx road is completly white on my mac, like NaN or inf blowout, but same track looks fine on the default renderer. can u figure out whats going on in the wgx path

Game froze on a single frame partway through a lap when running the WebGPU backend, and afterwards the log says the device was lost. Nothing recovers and the canvas stays dead instead of dropping back to the WebGL2 renderer. Diagnose why.

I edited the shadow pass in js/render/webgpu/wgx-shadow.js and want to be sure the WGSL still validates, including the path where rg11b10ufloat-renderable is unavailable. Run the right validation in this container and report what it finds.

I set the backend to webgpu but the HUD looks identical to WebGL2 and I suspect it silently fell back without telling anyone. How can I prove which backend is really running and find why the WGX init bailed out, including MSAA or HDR texture-format rejections?

On the WebGL2 GLX backend the canvas goes dark after boot and the console prints GL_INVALID_OPERATION from a uniform-array light upload. Track down the bad call in the GLX renderer and fix the shader uniform handling.

On the WebGPU renderer the tarmac shows the wrong colour and looks garbled, like the material layers are swapped: the kerbs pick up the grass texture. Check the baked pack MAT layer mapping and matTexMix, then fix it.

Night races look washed out like daytime and the floodlights never switch on, whichever renderer I pick including WebGPU. Work out why the dusk and night lighting gate is not firing and tune the exposure and ambient knobs.

On the default three.js backend the cars render see-through and the shadow pass flickers on my laptop, but apex26.gfxBackend=webgl2 looks fine. Work out whether TLX is falling back or the canvas alpha is wrong, and check gpuErrors on the three backend.
